## Statistical modelling

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(tidyverse)
theme_set(theme_light())
library(brms)
library(bayesplot)

```

![](/img/data-model.png){fig-align="center"}

## Gaussian models

$$y \sim Gaussian(\mu, \sigma)$$

```{r}
#| label: gauss
#| layout-ncol: 2

x <- seq(-10, 20, length.out = 1000)

means <- c(0, -5, 10)
sd_fixed <- 2

df_means <- crossing(x = x, mean = means) |> 
  mutate(
    y = dnorm(x, mean = mean, sd = sd_fixed),
    mean = factor(mean)
  ) |> 
  arrange(mean, x)

ggplot(df_means, aes(x = x, y = y, color = mean)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = element_blank(), y = "Density", caption = "SD = 2.")

sds <- c(1, 2, 4)
mean_fixed <- 5

df_sds <- crossing(x = x, SD = sds) |> 
  mutate(
    y = dnorm(x, mean = mean_fixed, sd = SD),
    SD = factor(SD)
  ) |> 
  arrange(SD, x)

ggplot(df_sds, aes(x = x, y = y, color = SD)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Density", caption = "Mean = 5.")

```

## Simulate Gaussian data

::: {style="text-align: center;"}
`rnorm(n, mean, sd)`
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
- `n`: number of obs to generate
- `mean`: mean of the Gaussian distribution
- `sd`: SD of the Gaussian distribution
:::

. . .

```{r}
#| label: f0
#| echo: true

set.seed(812)
f0 <- rnorm(200, 125, 25) |> round()

f0[1:10]
```

## f0 density

```{r}
#| label: f0-plot
#| fig-align: center

ggplot() +
  aes(f0) +
  geom_density(fill = "darkgreen", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_rug(alpha = 0.25) +
  labs(x = "f0 (Hz)")
```

## Simulation vs estimation

<br><br>

::::::: columns
:::: column
::: {style="text-align: center;"}
**SIMULATION**
:::

![](../img/flaticon/simulation.png){fig-align="center" height="100px"}

You have $\mu, \sigma$ and you generate $y$.
::::

:::: {.column .fragment}
::: {style="text-align: center;"}
**ESTIMATION**
:::

![](../img/flaticon/earth.png){fig-align="center" height="100px"}

You have $y$ and you estimate $\mu$ and $\sigma$.
::::
:::::::

::: aside
[<a href="https://www.flaticon.com/free-icons/simulation" title="simulation icons">Simulation icons created by Flat Icons - Flaticon</a>. <a href="https://www.flaticon.com/free-icons/world" title="world icons">World icons created by Freepik - Flaticon</a>]{style="font-size: 8px;"}
:::

::: notes
When you simulate data, you know the population mean and SD.
In research, you don't.
You just have observations.

Statistical modelling allows you to estimate the mean and SD of the population from the sample.
This is statistical inference.
**Bayesian Gaussian models** do exactly that: estimate mean and SD.
:::

## Gaussian model of f0

$$\begin{align}
f0 & \sim Gaussian(\mu, \sigma)\\
\mu & = ...\\
\sigma & = ...
\end{align}$$

## Gaussian model of f0

$$\begin{align}
f0 & \sim Gaussian(\mu, \sigma)\\
\mu & = P_\mu\\
\sigma & = P_\sigma
\end{align}$$

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
$P$ is a generic **posterior probability distribution**.
:::

## Gaussian model of f0: brms

```{r}
#| label: f0-bm
#| echo: true

f0_tib <- tibble(f0 = f0)

library(brms)

f0_bm <- brm(
  f0 ~ 1,
  family = gaussian,
  data = f0_tib,
  file = "cache/f0_bm"
)
```

## Gaussian model of height: posteriors

```{r}
#| label: f0-bm-plot
#| fig-align: center

mcmc_dens(f0_bm, pars = c("b_Intercept", "sigma"),
  facet_args = list(
    labeller = labeller(
      .default = as_labeller(c(b_Intercept = "mu", sigma = "sigma"))
    )
  )
)
```

## Posterior summary

```{r}
#| label: f0-bm-summary
#| echo: true

posterior_summary(f0_bm, probs = c(0.1, 0.9))[1:2,] |> round()
```

## A bit harder: N = 5

```{r}
#| label: f0-bm-small
#| echo: true

set.seed(4256)
f0_tib <- tibble(f0 = sample(f0, 5))

f0_bm_small <- brm(
  f0 ~ 1,
  family = gaussian,
  data = f0_tib,
  file = "cache/f0_bm_small"
)
```

## A bit harder: N = 5

```{r}
#| label: f0-bm-small-plot
#| fig-align: center

mcmc_dens(f0_bm_small, pars = c("b_Intercept", "sigma"),
  facet_args = list(
    labeller = labeller(
      .default = as_labeller(c(b_Intercept = "mu", sigma = "sigma"))
    )
  )
)
```

## A bit harder: N = 5

```{r}
#| label: f0-bm-small-summary
#| echo: true

posterior_summary(f0_bm_small, probs = c(0.1, 0.9))[1:2,] |> round()
```
